validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: Confirmed real. 'UBTG' is a genuine Saudi Aramco corridor designation (Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas line), part of the Master Gas System. Independent, verifier-passing sources confirm the Aramco MGS as an extensive processed-gas trunk network connecting the Berri, Uthmaniyah, Hawiyah, Juaymah and Shedgum gas plants in the Eastern Province (OGN News; Saudipedia Hawiyah Gas Plant). The pipeline-specific characteristics (length 249 km, telescoping diameters 56/36/38/40/42 in) match a peer-reviewed paper titled 'Electromagnetic Interference Caused By A High Voltage Transmission Network On Buried Pipelines & Communication Cables' (ResearchGate publication 291522747), which contains a table literally titled 'UBTG-1 Pipeline Characteristics' and studies Aramco buried pipelines near the 380 kV Shedgum-Qurayyah lines in the Eastern Province. That paper is the apparent origin of GEM's numbers, but it is hosted only on ResearchGate/Academia.edu, both of which return HTTP 403 to scripts/url_verifier.py, so I cannot stage its URL. This is the ONLY independent confirmation of the exact specs, so the specs are at best medium and effectively single-sourced for citation purposes. NOT a hallucination, but the GEM-only-derived web echo is heavy: nearly all generic web hits ('249 km, diameters 56,36,38,40,42, Saudi Aramco') trace straight back to gem.wiki. CLASSIFICATION: Correctly a dry/sales GAS transmission trunk line, not NGL and not a gathering line - the Master Gas System carries processed sales gas (OGN, Saudipedia). Fuel=Gas confirmed; Owner=Saudi Aramco confirmed (whole MGS is Aramco-owned/operated). DUPLICATE CONCERN (see separate validity object): P1899 'UBTG-1-Berri 2' is 247 km with the identical diameter set - almost certainly the parallel/twin line of the same corridor or a double-count of one telescoping pipe; flagged below.

validity.researcher_notes: P1898 'UBTG-1-Berri' (249 km, dia 56,36,38,40,42 in) and P1899 'UBTG-1-Berri 2' (247 km, dia 56,36,38,40,42 in) are near-identical in length (within ~1%) and carry the EXACT same diameter set, same endpoints (both Saudi Arabia, Berri terminus), same owner (Aramco), same status (operating). The source paper presents a single 'UBTG-1 Pipeline Characteristics' table describing one telescoping line. GEM has additionally fragmented the corridor into km-marker rows (P1900 UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916, P1910/P1911 UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56 [a '1' and a '2'], P1912 Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0). The '1' vs '2' twinning pattern (mirrored again at P1910/P1911) suggests the database is double-entering each physical telescoping line as two rows, or splitting one line into a chain of km-segments AND keeping a whole-line row. This is a likely duplicate/segment-double-count and should be reconciled by a human before the spec numbers are trusted. I could NOT find any independent source distinguishing a 'UBTG-1' line 1 from a line 2.
